justifications.r1: Cheap 1-2 CMC ramp spells (Birds of Paradise, Avacyn's Pilgrim, Sol Ring, Nature's Lore, Three Visits, Farseek, Rampant Growth) deploy Turn 4 Karametra, whose continuous land-fetch triggers on every creature cast generate massive mana acceleration.
justifications.r2: Solid B-tier card flow powered by The Great Henge, Sylvan Library, Guardian Project, Tribute to the World Tree, Esper Sentinel, and Battle Angels of Tyr.
justifications.a1: B-tier selection and redundancy anchored by Worldly Tutor and Eladamri's Call finding key Angels and finishers.
justifications.a2: Reaches engine readiness by Turn 4 via reliable early ramp into Karametra, God of Harvests.
justifications.p1: Threat onset hits by Turn 6 as high-impact threats (Avenger of Zendikar, Righteous Valkyrie, Lyra Dawnbringer, Elesh Norn) establish massive board presence.
justifications.p2: Requires 2 opponent response cycles after Turn 6 onset to close out games across the pod via aerial combat and Landfall overruns (Turn 8 kill).
justifications.p3: High-flying Angel threats and growing Landfall tokens telegraph lethal damage across multiple attack steps.
justifications.i1: B-tier reactive disruption suite featuring Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Beast Within, Generous Gift, Farewell, and Austere Command.
justifications.i2: B-tier proactive denial anchored by Aura Shards repeatedly wiping opposing artifacts/enchantments, Linvala shutting down activated abilities, Authority of the Consuls tapping creatures, and Angelic Arbiter / Archangel of Tithes imposing attack taxes.
justifications.s1: Premier A-tier plan shielding via Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Avacyn, Angel of Hope, Shalai, Voice of Plenty, Sigarda, Font of Blessings, and Serra's Emissary.
justifications.s2: A-tier engine recovery powered by Emeria Shepherd recurring nonland permanents on Plains drops, Eternal Witness, Bala Ged Recovery, and resilient indestructible permanents.
justifications.s3: High independence (A-tier): the 99 functions as an autonomous Angel tribal beatdown and Landfall engine even without Karametra.

overview: This deck is a Selesnya Midrange strategy combining Angel tribal synergies with Karametra's explosive land-ramp engine. In the early game, cheap ramp spells accelerate Karametra onto the battlefield by Turn 4. Once Karametra is established, every subsequent creature cast fetches a Forest or Plains directly onto the battlefield, creating rapid mana acceleration and thinning the library. In the mid-to-late game, this abundant mana powers out high-impact threats such as Avenger of Zendikar, Righteous Valkyrie, Lyra Dawnbringer, and Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite. The deck closes games through overwhelming aerial combat, often boosted by Akroma's Will or Landfall counters. Robust protection pieces like Heroic Intervention, Shalai, Voice of Plenty, and Sigarda, Font of Blessings shield the board against opposing interaction.

core_strategy: Accelerate early with 1-2 CMC ramp spells like Nature's Lore and Birds of Paradise to cast Karametra, God of Harvests by Turn 4.
Trigger Karametra repeatedly by casting mid-cost creatures and utility Angels, pulling lands from the library to fuel big-mana plays.
Deploy board-dominating threats like Avenger of Zendikar, Righteous Valkyrie, or Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite around Turn 6.
Overwhelm the table with large flying creatures and finish opponents with an alpha strike backed by Akroma's Will or wide Landfall buffs.

keep: Hands with 3-4 lands and at least one 1-2 CMC ramp spell to guarantee a Turn 4 Karametra, ideally with a cheap creature or draw engine to follow up.
avoid: Hands heavy with 5+ CMC Angels and no early ramp, or hands lacking basic land access to start the engine.

key_tips: Keep Karametra's devotion below seven early if you expect creature exile removal; an indestructible enchantment is much harder for opponents to interact with.
Hold Heroic Intervention or Akroma's Will open once your aerial engine is assembled to protect your board from sweepers.
Prioritize fetching Plains cards when Emeria Shepherd is in hand or on the battlefield to trigger direct-to-battlefield reanimation.

critical: Mass exile effects such as Farewell bypass Karametra's indestructible keyword and remove the deck's board and graveyard in one blow.
moderate: Lack of stack-based countermagic leaves the deck vulnerable to fast noncreature combo decks and early game-ending spells.
Reliance on natural draws for noncreature draw engines can cause the deck to run out of gas if early creatures are removed.
minor: Nonbasic land destruction or search-stax effects like Aven Mindcensor can slow down Karametra's land-fetching triggers.
